neighbours.label: the punctuation or digit right after a journal title and volume number in a bibliographic citation ('History Today 58.1 (', 'Review 50 (1976)')
fire: Carter, Helen. "Salt and Empire." Journal of Economic History 37 (1977): 201-219.
Novak, Peter. "The Lost Charters." Slavic Review 61.2 (Summer 2002): 88-104.
Okafor, Ngozi. "Markets of the Delta." African Studies Quarterly 19 (Fall 1988): 5-27.
Grant, Susan. "Reading the Psalms." Theology Today 44.3 (October 1987): 310-325.
Ito, Kenji. "Bridges Under Load." International Journal of Civil Engineering 31 (4): 455-470.
Wells, Martin. "Whaling Ports." The New England Quarterly 72 (1999): 33-58.
Duarte, Ana. "Rivers and Borders." Hispanic American Historical Review 83.1 (February 2003): 1-30.
Byrne, Colm. "Monastic Schools." Irish Historical Studies 26 (May 1989): 140-162.
quiet: Helen Carter wrote about salt and empire in 1977, in an essay of about nineteen pages.
Peter Novak found 61 lost charters (most of them damaged) in the summer of 2002.
Ngozi Okafor visited 19 markets of the delta (in the fall of 1988) with five students.
Susan Grant read 44 psalms aloud (in October 1987) to a class of three hundred.
Kenji Ito tested 31 bridges under load (4 of them failed) over 455 days.
Martin Wells counted 72 whaling ships (in 1999) from the old port records.
Ana Duarte mapped 83 rivers and borders (by February 2003) for the first atlas.
Colm Byrne taught at 26 monastic schools (until May 1989) across the island.

notes: Card: ' (' x10, '.', ',' after journal name + volume in citations; a second, smaller sense is ' into' ... eyes (not covered by this label). Probes: 'Journal of Ancient History 42 (1998)' 0.58, 'Machine Learning Review 12.3 (May 2015)' 0.58, "'Nature Today, March 3, 2004" 0.42; 'founded in 1998 and has 42 volumes' 0.02; 'into her eyes' 0.48, 'stared into the fire' 0.38.
